answer: Each agent locks a 60-credit opal bond to join a grove registry; each signed statement carries a sequence number. A public beacon posts the ordered log, so conflicting statements sharing one number are visible to all. Any peer can file an equivocation proof; the bond burns and the reporter keeps 20 credits. Forging 1,000 identities costs 60,000 locked plus 15,000 in fees against a 40,000 pool. An honest agent files once, pays 15, keeps its bond.
